author: Epiphanius of Salamis
occasion: The work provides a catalogue of the seventy disciples and the twelve apostles, recording their names, offices, and traditions about their deaths or later careers.
argument: The text first lists the seventy disciples, identifying many as bishops of various cities and noting how some died or fell away. It then lists the twelve apostles, giving alternate names and family details. The catalogue closes by explaining the identity of James the brother of the Lord and the meaning of the name Jonah.

outline.move: The title and opening entries list the first disciples, beginning with James the brother of the Lord and continuing through several of the seven deacons and other early figures.
The catalogue continues with disciples mentioned by Paul in Romans, assigning many of them bishoprics and recording traditions about their deaths.
Further disciples are listed, including those who later fell into heresy or abandoned the faith, with their assigned sees.
The final disciples are listed, followed by the names of the twelve apostles, their alternate names, and a note on James the brother of the Lord and the meaning of Jonah.

key_terms.sense: Bishop, the overseer of a local church.
Apostle, one of the twelve or a commissioned messenger.
Deacon, one of the seven appointed to serve in Acts.
To bear witness, especially by dying for the faith.
To hold false doctrine or fall into heresy.
First martyr, a title for Stephen.
The gospel, the good news of Jesus Christ.
Brother of the Lord, a relative of Jesus.
Chief or leader, used of Peter.
Sons of thunder, the meaning of Boanerges.

scripture: The author cites the Acts of the Apostles, the Gospel of Luke, the Gospel of Matthew, the Gospel of Mark, Paul's letters to the Romans, Corinthians, and Timothy. Modern citations should use standard English Bible book names and chapter/verse numbering.
uncertain: The exact date of composition is not stated in the text.
The identity of the addressee is not indicated.
Some place names, such as 'Ne Potiolis' and 'Conia', are uncertain.
The precise relationship between the various lists and their sources is not explained.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Crescens ... Bishop of Chalcedon in Gaul
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Κρήσκης, οὗ μέμνηται ὁ ἀπόστολος Παῦλος ἐν τῇ πρὸς Τιμόθεον δευτέρᾳ ἐπιστολῇ, ὁ καὶ ἐπίσκοπος Χαλκηδόνος τῶν ἐν Γαλλίαις γενόμενος ἐκεῖ ἐκήρυξε τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ
_unresolved_facts.fix: Bishop of Chalcedon in the Gauls (Γαλλίαις), preached the gospel there, martyred under Trajan and buried there.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Clement ... first from the Gentiles and Greeks to believe in Christ, bishop of Sardica
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὃς καὶ πρῶτος ἐξ ἐθνῶν καὶ Ἑλλήνων ἐπίστευσεν εἰς Χριστόν, ἐπίσκοπος Σαρδικῆς ἐγένετο
_unresolved_facts.fix: First of the Gentiles and Greeks to believe in Christ, bishop of Sardica.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Aristarchus ... one of three who suffered with Paul in all his persecutions, finally perfected by martyrdom with him under Nero, beheaded with him
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Οὗτοι οἱ τρεῖς ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς διωγμοῖς τοῦ ἀποστόλου Παύλου συγκακοπαθήσαντες αὐτῷ, τελευταῖοι καὶ διὰ μαρτυρίου σὺν ἐκείνῳ ἐτελειώθησαν ὑπὸ Νέρωνος τὰς κεφαλὰς σὺν ἐκείνῳ ἀποτμηθέντες. Τούτοις συναριθμουμένων καὶ Μάρκου καὶ Λουκᾶ τοῦ εὐαγγελιστοῦ ὁμοῦ
_unresolved_facts.fix: One of three who suffered with Paul in all his persecutions, finally perfected by martyrdom with him under Nero, beheaded with him. Mark and Luke the evangelist are also counted together with these.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Pudens ... one of three who suffered with Paul in all his persecutions, finally perfected by martyrdom with him under Nero, beheaded with him
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Οὗτοι οἱ τρεῖς ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς διωγμοῖς τοῦ ἀποστόλου Παύλου συγκακοπαθήσαντες αὐτῷ, τελευταῖοι καὶ διὰ μαρτυρίου σὺν ἐκείνῳ ἐτελειώθησαν ὑπὸ Νέρωνος τὰς κεφαλὰς σὺν ἐκείνῳ ἀποτμηθέντες. Τούτοις συναριθμουμένων καὶ Μάρκου καὶ Λουκᾶ τοῦ εὐαγγελιστοῦ ὁμοῦ
_unresolved_facts.fix: One of three who suffered with Paul in all his persecutions, finally perfected by martyrdom with him under Nero, beheaded with him. Mark and Luke the evangelist are also counted together with these.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Thaddaeus ... Called Lebbaeus by Matthew, Judas son of James by Luke, and Levi sitting at the tax office by Mark
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Θαδδαῖος, οὗτος παρὰ μὲν τῷ Ματθαίῳ Λεββαῖος καλεῖται, παρὰ δὲ τῷ Λουκᾷ Ἰούδας Ἰακώβου, παρὰ δὲ τῷ Μάρκῳ Λευὶς καθήμενος παρὰ τὸ τελώνιον
_unresolved_facts.fix: Called Lebbaeus by Matthew, Judas son of James by Luke, and Levi the tax collector (sitting at the tax office) by Mark.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Joseph Barsabbas ... Also called Justus, candidate for apostleship with Matthias, bishop of Eleutheropolis
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἰωσὴφ ὁ λεγόμενος καὶ Ἰοῦστος καὶ Βαρσαββᾶς, οὗ μέμνηται Λουκᾶς ἐν ταῖς πράξεσι τῶν ἀποστόλων ὡς συγκληρωθέντος τῷ Ματθίᾳ
_unresolved_facts.fix: Also called Justus and Barsabbas, mentioned by Luke in Acts as having been chosen by lot with Matthias.

_unresolved_facts.claim: James the brother of the Lord ... First bishop of Jerusalem, called the Just, stoned by Jews
_unresolved_facts.fix: First bishop of Jerusalem, called the Just, stoned by Jews in Jerusalem itself, fell asleep and was buried there in the temple near the priests.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Timothy ... preached in Illyricum and Greece
_unresolved_facts.fix: Bishop of Ephesus, beginning from Ephesus preached the gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ in Illyricum and all Greece; there he died and was buried gloriously.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Barnabas ... first preached Christ in Rome; later became bishop of Mediolanum (Milan)
_unresolved_facts.fix: Served the word with Paul, first preached Christ in Rome; later became bishop of Mediolanum. (Note: The text says μετέπειτα δὲ Μεδιολάνων ἐπίσκοπος ἐγένετο, with no explicit 'later' temporal marker for the Rome preaching.)

_unresolved_facts.claim: Olympas ... Martyred in Rome together with Peter the chief, beheaded
_unresolved_facts.fix: Martyred in Rome together with Peter the chief, having his head cut off.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Rhodion ... Likewise in Rome with Peter and Olympas was perfected by martyrdom, he too beheaded
_unresolved_facts.fix: Likewise in Rome with Peter and Olympas was perfected by martyrdom, he too having his head cut off.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Demas ... Abandoned the gospel, became a priest of idols in Thessalonica
_unresolved_facts.fix: Loving the present age, abandoned the evangelical word, and in Thessalonica became a priest of idols.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Mark also called John ... Bishop of Byblos
_unresolved_facts.fix: Mark also called John, mentioned by Luke in Acts, bishop of Byblos.

_unresolved_facts.fix: Also called Simon and Cephas and Symeon; brother of Andrew, son of Anna.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Andrew ... Brother of Peter
_unresolved_facts.fix: Brother of Peter, son of Anna.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The catalogue closes by explaining the identity of James the brother of the Lord and the meaning of the name Jonah
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἰάκωβος ὁ καλούμενος ἀδελφὸς τοῦ κυρίου, ποῖος ἦν ὁ γενόμενος ἐπίσκοπος Ἱερουσαλήμ, ὁ ἐπονομαζόμενος δίκαιος, ὁ εἷς ἦν υἱὸς Ζεβεδαίου καὶ ὁ ἕτερος Ἀλφαίου, καὶ ὁ ἄλλος τοῦ Ἰωσὴφ τοῦ μνήστορος, ὡς ἔλεγον Ἰουδαῖοι... Ἰωνᾶς δὲ ἑρμηνεύεται περιστερά.
_unresolved_facts.fix: The catalogue closes by explaining which James was called brother of the Lord (distinguishing him from James son of Zebedee, James son of Alphaeus, and James son of Joseph the betrothed, as the Jews said), noting family relationships among the apostles, and stating that Jonah is interpreted as dove.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The title and opening entries list the first disciples, beginning with James the brother of the Lord and continuing through several of the seven deacons and other early figures
_unresolved_facts.fix: The title and opening entries list the first disciples, beginning with James the brother of the Lord and continuing through Timothy, Titus, Barnabas, Ananias, the seven deacons (Stephen, Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Simon, Parmenas, Nicolaus), Cleopas/Symeon, Silas, and others.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The catalogue continues with disciples mentioned by Paul in Romans, assigning many of them bishoprics and recording traditions about their deaths
_unresolved_facts.fix: The catalogue continues with disciples mentioned by Paul in Romans, assigning many of them bishoprics and recording traditions about their appointments and deaths.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Further disciples are listed, including those who later fell into heresy or abandoned the faith, with their assigned sees
_unresolved_facts.fix: Further disciples are listed, including Tertius, Erastus, Phygelus, Hermogenes, and Demas—three of whom (Phygelus, Hermogenes, Demas) fell into heresy or abandoned the faith—with their assigned sees and additional details about their fates.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The final disciples are listed, followed by the names of the twelve apostles, their alternate names, and a note on James the brother of the Lord and the meaning of Jonah
_unresolved_facts.fix: The final disciples are listed (including Aristarchus, Pudens, and Trophimus, with Mark and Luke also counted with them), followed by the names of the twelve apostles, their alternate names, family relationships, and notes on which James was called brother of the Lord and that Jonah means dove.
